title: The Latent Curve Model with Structured Residuals
text: latent curve model structured residuals (LCM-SR) combines two ideas (Curran et al., 2014). Take alcohol use depressive symptoms measured year adolescents. adolescent follows straight-line trajectory variable, intercept slope, linear growth curve model. occasion, adolescent also trajectory, deviations, called structured residuals, carry next occasion affect . growth part describes individuals differ long-term change; residual part describes within-person dynamics around , autoregressive cross-lagged effects. LCM-SR usually fitted structural equation model (SEM). can also written state space model combining state space forms linear growth curve model vector autoregressive model: levels slopes two trajectories two residuals latent states. tutorial three things: writes LCM-SR state space model. simulates data model SimSSMFixed(). fits model simulated data state space model dynr OpenMx structural equation model (SEM) lavaan OpenMx, compares every set estimates values used simulate data. prior knowledge state space models needed. vignette linear growth curve model explains growth part detail.

1}} \\     \eta_{2_{, t - 1}} \\     \eta_{3_{, t - 1}} \\     \eta_{4_{, t - 1}} \\     \eta_{5_{, t - 1}} \\     \eta_{6_{, t - 1}} \\   \end{array}   \right)   +   \left(   \begin{array}{c}     0 \\     0 \\     0 \\     0 \\     \zeta_{5_{, t}} \\     \zeta_{6_{, t}} \\   \end{array}   \right),   \quad   \mathrm{}   \quad   \left(   \begin{array}{c}     \zeta_{5_{, t}} \\     \zeta_{6_{, t}} \\   \end{array}   \right)   \sim   \mathcal{N}   \left(   \mathbf{0},   \left(   \begin{array}{cc}     \psi_{55} & \psi_{56} \\     \psi_{65} & \psi_{66} \\   \end{array}   \right)   \right) . words, first four rows linear growth curve model variable: level occasion previous level plus slope, slope stays , process noise. last two rows vector autoregressive model residuals: \beta_{55} \beta_{66} autoregressive effects, much deviation trajectory carries next occasion, \beta_{56} \beta_{65} cross-lagged effects: \beta_{56} effect deviation second variable deviation first variable next occasion, \beta_{65} reverse. \psi_{55}, \psi_{66}, \psi_{56} variances covariance new part deviations. initial condition holds means, variances, covariances intercepts slopes (levels first occasion intercepts), variances covariance residuals first occasion. residuals mean zero, deviations trajectories, uncorrelated intercepts slopes.

title: The Latent Curve Model with Structured Residuals
text: OpenMx (Neale et al., 2016) fits state space model Kalman filter (OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(); Hunter (2018)). matrices names used engineering: transition matrix \boldsymbol{\beta}, B holds intercepts dynamic model, C loading matrix \boldsymbol{\Lambda}, D holds intercepts measurement model, Q process noise covariance matrix, R measurement error covariance matrix. parameter labels dynr names; dynr, label used two places one shared parameter, starting values population values. Two details differ dynr. First, OpenMx reads data single time series. start filter first occasion every individual, individual gets group, groups use matrices one parent model, every individual parameters. Second, OpenMx starts filter one occasion first row, first row state mean \mathbf{} \mathbf{x}_{0} + \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} state covariance \mathbf{} \mathbf{P}_{0} \mathbf{}^{\prime} + \mathbf{Q}, constant input \mathbf{u} = 1. Setting \mathbf{x}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\mu}_{0} - \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} \right) \mathbf{P}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{0} - \mathbf{Q} \right) \left( \mathbf{}^{-1} \right)^{\prime} gives first occasion initial condition model, likelihood dynr. needs invertible \mathbf{}, holds . two helper functions every vignette package. MxMat() makes OpenMx matrix values dynr-style labels ("fixed" marks fixed element), FitMxSSM() builds groups fits model. matrices model, dynr labels (params_sigma0 params_psi label matrices made dynr). measurement error (R zero).
code: MxMat <- function(values, labels, name) {   values <- as.matrix(values)   labels <- matrix(     data = labels,     nrow = nrow(values),     ncol = ncol(values)   )   free <- labels != "fixed"   labels[!free] <- NA   OpenMx::mxMatrix(     type = "Full",     values = values,     free = free,     labels = labels,     name = name   ) } FitMxSSM <- function(data, observed, matrices, name) {   # the groups refer to the matrices of the parent model   shared <- function(x) {     paste0(name, ".", x)   }   expectation <- OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(     A = shared("A"),     B = shared("B"),     C = shared("C"),     D = shared("D"),     Q = shared("Q"),     R = shared("R"),     x0 = shared("x0"),     P0 = shared("P0"),     u = shared("u")   )   # OpenMx needs the names of the observed variables and of the states on C   for (i in seq_along(matrices)) {     if (matrices[[i]]$name == "C") {       dimnames(matrices[[i]]) <- list(         observed,         paste0("eta_", seq_len(ncol(matrices[[i]]$values)))       )     }   }   persons <- split(     x = data[, observed, drop = FALSE],     f = data[, "id"]   )   groups <- paste0("id_", names(persons))   submodels <- lapply(     X = seq_along(persons),     FUN = function(i) {       OpenMx::mxModel(         name = groups[i],         expectation,         OpenMx::mxFitFunctionML(),         OpenMx::mxData(           observed = persons[[i]],           type = "raw"         )       )     }   )   model <- OpenMx::mxModel(     name = name,     matrices,     OpenMx::mxMatrix(       type = "Unit",       nrow = 1,       ncol = 1,       name = "u"     ),     # the first occasion gets the initial condition of the model     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (mu0 - B %*% u),       name = "x0"     ),     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (sigma0 - Q) %*% t(solve(A)),       name = "P0"     ),     submodels,     OpenMx::mxFitFunctionMultigroup(groups = groups)   )   # retries from perturbed starting values only if the first run fails   OpenMx::mxTryHard(     model = model,     extraTries = 5,     silent = TRUE   ) } labels_beta <- matrix(data = "fixed", nrow = p, ncol = p) labels_beta[5:6, 5:6] <- c("beta_5_5", "beta_6_5", "beta_5_6", "beta_6_6") mx_matrices <- list(   MxMat(values = beta, labels = labels_beta, name = "A"),   MxMat(values = alpha, labels = "fixed", name = "B"),   MxMat(values = lambda, labels = "fixed", name = "C"),   MxMat(values = nu, labels = "fixed", name = "D"),   MxMat(values = psi, labels = params_psi, name = "Q"),   MxMat(values = theta, labels = "fixed", name = "R"),   MxMat(     values = mu0,     labels = c(       "mu0_1_1", "mu0_2_1", "mu0_3_1", "mu0_4_1", "fixed", "fixed"     ),     name = "mu0"   ),   MxMat(values = sigma0, labels = params_sigma0, name = "sigma0") ) fit_mx_ssm <- FitMxSSM(   data = data,   observed = c("y1", "y2"),   matrices = mx_matrices,   name = "lcm_sr" ) #>  Beginning initial fit attempt Fit attempt 0, fit=127121.905417101, new current best! (was 127140.637002899)                                                                               #>  #>  Solution found! title: The Bivariate Dual Change Score Model
text: Latent change score models describe change (McArdle, 2009). Take vocabulary reading comprehension measured year children. one occasion next, child’s vocabulary changes. dual change score model, change two sources: constant amount child gains every year (slope), amount depends child stood year (self-feedback). bivariate model, change one variable can also depend previous level variable (coupling), example, children larger vocabulary gain reading comprehension. dual change score model usually fitted structural equation model (SEM). can also written state space model: true levels two variables latent states, slopes latent states never change. tutorial three things: writes bivariate dual change score model state space model. simulates data model SimSSMFixed(). fits model simulated data state space model dynr OpenMx structural equation model (SEM) lavaan OpenMx, compares every set estimates values used simulate data. prior knowledge state space models needed.

title: The Bivariate Dual Change Score Model
text: measurement model given \left(   \begin{array}{c}     Y_{1_{, t}} \\     Y_{2_{, t}} \\   \end{array}   \right)   =   \left(   \begin{array}{cccc}     1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\     0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\   \end{array}   \right)   \left(   \begin{array}{c}     \eta_{1_{, t}} \\     \eta_{2_{, t}} \\     \eta_{3_{, t}} \\     \eta_{4_{, t}} \\   \end{array}   \right)   +   \left(   \begin{array}{c}     \varepsilon_{1_{, t}} \\     \varepsilon_{2_{, t}} \\   \end{array}   \right),   \quad   \mathrm{}   \quad   \left(   \begin{array}{c}     \varepsilon_{1_{, t}} \\     \varepsilon_{2_{, t}} \\   \end{array}   \right)   \sim   \mathcal{N}   \left(   \mathbf{0},   \left(   \begin{array}{cc}     \theta_{11} & 0 \\     0 & \theta_{22} \\   \end{array}   \right)   \right) Y_{1_{, t}} Y_{2_{, t}} two observed variables time t individual , \eta_{1_{, t}} \eta_{2_{, t}} true levels, \eta_{3_{, t}} \eta_{4_{, t}} slopes, \theta_{11} \theta_{22} measurement error variances. words, observed score true level plus measurement error. slopes loadings 0: affect scores change true levels. change true level first variable occasion t - 1 occasion t \Delta \eta_{1_{, t}}   =   \eta_{3_{, t - 1}}   +   b_{1} \eta_{1_{, t - 1}}   +   g_{12} \eta_{2_{, t - 1}} , similarly second variable, \Delta \eta_{2_{, t}} = \eta_{4_{, t - 1}} + b_{2} \eta_{2_{, t - 1}} + g_{21} \eta_{1_{, t - 1}}. true level occasion t previous true level plus change, \eta_{1_{, t}} = \eta_{1_{, t - 1}} + \Delta \eta_{1_{, t}}. Writing change level gives dynamic structure \left(   \begin{array}{c}     \eta_{1_{, t}} \\     \eta_{2_{, t}} \\     \eta_{3_{, t}} \\     \eta_{4_{, t}} \\   \end{array}   \right)   =   \left(   \begin{array}{cccc}     1 + b_{1} & g_{12} & 1 & 0 \\     g_{21} & 1 + b_{2} & 0 & 1 \\     0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\     0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\   \end{array}   \right)   \left(   \begin{array}{c}     \eta_{1_{, t - 1}} \\     \eta_{2_{, t - 1}} \\     \eta_{3_{, t - 1}} \\     \eta_{4_{, t - 1}} \\   \end{array}   \right) . words, b_{1} b_{2} self-feedback effects: negative value means individuals stand higher gain less, levels level time. g_{12} coupling second variable first: positive value means higher level second variable followed larger gain first. g_{21} reverse. slopes stay time. applications model, process noise: initial levels slopes set, true trajectories fixed. initial condition holds means, variances, covariances initial true levels slopes, \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, 0}   \sim   \mathcal{N}   \left(   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{0},   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{0}   \right) . example, positive covariance initial level slope variable means individuals start higher also tend gain year.

title: The Bivariate Dual Change Score Model
text: OpenMx (Neale et al., 2016) fits state space model Kalman filter (OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(); Hunter (2018)). matrices names used engineering: transition matrix \boldsymbol{\beta}, B holds intercepts dynamic model, C loading matrix \boldsymbol{\Lambda}, D holds intercepts measurement model, Q process noise covariance matrix, R measurement error covariance matrix. parameter labels dynr names; dynr, label used two places one shared parameter, starting values population values. Two details differ dynr. First, OpenMx reads data single time series. start filter first occasion every individual, individual gets group, groups use matrices one parent model, every individual parameters. Second, OpenMx starts filter one occasion first row, first row state mean \mathbf{} \mathbf{x}_{0} + \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} state covariance \mathbf{} \mathbf{P}_{0} \mathbf{}^{\prime} + \mathbf{Q}, constant input \mathbf{u} = 1. Setting \mathbf{x}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\mu}_{0} - \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} \right) \mathbf{P}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{0} - \mathbf{Q} \right) \left( \mathbf{}^{-1} \right)^{\prime} gives first occasion initial condition model, likelihood dynr. needs invertible \mathbf{}, holds . two helper functions every vignette package. MxMat() makes OpenMx matrix values dynr-style labels ("fixed" marks fixed element), FitMxSSM() builds groups fits model. matrices model, dynr labels. transition matrix fixed part (level carries adds slope) plus self-feedback coupling effects, algebra, sum two. process noise (Q zero).
code: MxMat <- function(values, labels, name) {   values <- as.matrix(values)   labels <- matrix(     data = labels,     nrow = nrow(values),     ncol = ncol(values)   )   free <- labels != "fixed"   labels[!free] <- NA   OpenMx::mxMatrix(     type = "Full",     values = values,     free = free,     labels = labels,     name = name   ) } FitMxSSM <- function(data, observed, matrices, name) {   # the groups refer to the matrices of the parent model   shared <- function(x) {     paste0(name, ".", x)   }   expectation <- OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(     A = shared("A"),     B = shared("B"),     C = shared("C"),     D = shared("D"),     Q = shared("Q"),     R = shared("R"),     x0 = shared("x0"),     P0 = shared("P0"),     u = shared("u")   )   # OpenMx needs the names of the observed variables and of the states on C   for (i in seq_along(matrices)) {     if (matrices[[i]]$name == "C") {       dimnames(matrices[[i]]) <- list(         observed,         paste0("eta_", seq_len(ncol(matrices[[i]]$values)))       )     }   }   persons <- split(     x = data[, observed, drop = FALSE],     f = data[, "id"]   )   groups <- paste0("id_", names(persons))   submodels <- lapply(     X = seq_along(persons),     FUN = function(i) {       OpenMx::mxModel(         name = groups[i],         expectation,         OpenMx::mxFitFunctionML(),         OpenMx::mxData(           observed = persons[[i]],           type = "raw"         )       )     }   )   model <- OpenMx::mxModel(     name = name,     matrices,     OpenMx::mxMatrix(       type = "Unit",       nrow = 1,       ncol = 1,       name = "u"     ),     # the first occasion gets the initial condition of the model     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (mu0 - B %*% u),       name = "x0"     ),     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (sigma0 - Q) %*% t(solve(A)),       name = "P0"     ),     submodels,     OpenMx::mxFitFunctionMultigroup(groups = groups)   )   # retries from perturbed starting values only if the first run fails   OpenMx::mxTryHard(     model = model,     extraTries = 5,     silent = TRUE   ) } feedback <- matrix(data = 0, nrow = 4, ncol = 4) feedback[1:2, 1:2] <- c(b_1, g_2_1, g_1_2, b_2) labels_feedback <- matrix(data = "fixed", nrow = 4, ncol = 4) labels_feedback[1:2, 1:2] <- c("b_1", "g_2_1", "g_1_2", "b_2") labels_sigma0 <- matrix(   data = c(     "sigma0_1_1", "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_3_1", "sigma0_4_1",     "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_2_2", "sigma0_3_2", "sigma0_4_2",     "sigma0_3_1", "sigma0_3_2", "sigma0_3_3", "sigma0_4_3",     "sigma0_4_1", "sigma0_4_2", "sigma0_4_3", "sigma0_4_4"   ),   nrow = 4 ) mx_matrices <- list(   MxMat(values = beta - feedback, labels = "fixed", name = "carry"),   MxMat(values = feedback, labels = labels_feedback, name = "feedback"),   OpenMx::mxAlgebra(expression = carry + feedback, name = "A"),   MxMat(values = alpha, labels = "fixed", name = "B"),   MxMat(values = lambda, labels = "fixed", name = "C"),   MxMat(values = nu, labels = "fixed", name = "D"),   MxMat(values = psi, labels = "fixed", name = "Q"),   MxMat(     values = theta,     labels = c("theta_1_1", "fixed", "fixed", "theta_2_2"),     name = "R"   ),   MxMat(     values = mu0,     labels = c("mu0_1_1", "mu0_2_1", "mu0_3_1", "mu0_4_1"),     name = "mu0"   ),   MxMat(values = sigma0, labels = labels_sigma0, name = "sigma0") ) fit_mx_ssm <- FitMxSSM(   data = data,   observed = c("y1", "y2"),   matrices = mx_matrices,   name = "lcs" ) #>  Beginning initial fit attempt Fit attempt 0, fit=129790.546060362, new current best! title: The Linear Growth Curve Model
text: OpenMx (Neale et al., 2016) fits state space model Kalman filter (OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(); Hunter (2018)). matrices names used engineering: transition matrix \boldsymbol{\beta}, B holds intercepts dynamic model, C loading matrix \boldsymbol{\Lambda}, D holds intercepts measurement model, Q process noise covariance matrix, R measurement error covariance matrix. parameter labels dynr names; dynr, label used two places one shared parameter, starting values population values. Two details differ dynr. First, OpenMx reads data single time series. start filter first occasion every individual, individual gets group, groups use matrices one parent model, every individual parameters. Second, OpenMx starts filter one occasion first row, first row state mean \mathbf{} \mathbf{x}_{0} + \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} state covariance \mathbf{} \mathbf{P}_{0} \mathbf{}^{\prime} + \mathbf{Q}, constant input \mathbf{u} = 1. Setting \mathbf{x}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\mu}_{0} - \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} \right) \mathbf{P}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{0} - \mathbf{Q} \right) \left( \mathbf{}^{-1} \right)^{\prime} gives first occasion initial condition model, likelihood dynr. needs invertible \mathbf{}, holds . two helper functions every vignette package. MxMat() makes OpenMx matrix values dynr-style labels ("fixed" marks fixed element), FitMxSSM() builds groups fits model. matrices model, dynr labels. transition matrix carries intercept adds slope, process noise (Q zero).
code: MxMat <- function(values, labels, name) {   values <- as.matrix(values)   labels <- matrix(     data = labels,     nrow = nrow(values),     ncol = ncol(values)   )   free <- labels != "fixed"   labels[!free] <- NA   OpenMx::mxMatrix(     type = "Full",     values = values,     free = free,     labels = labels,     name = name   ) } FitMxSSM <- function(data, observed, matrices, name) {   # the groups refer to the matrices of the parent model   shared <- function(x) {     paste0(name, ".", x)   }   expectation <- OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(     A = shared("A"),     B = shared("B"),     C = shared("C"),     D = shared("D"),     Q = shared("Q"),     R = shared("R"),     x0 = shared("x0"),     P0 = shared("P0"),     u = shared("u")   )   # OpenMx needs the names of the observed variables and of the states on C   for (i in seq_along(matrices)) {     if (matrices[[i]]$name == "C") {       dimnames(matrices[[i]]) <- list(         observed,         paste0("eta_", seq_len(ncol(matrices[[i]]$values)))       )     }   }   persons <- split(     x = data[, observed, drop = FALSE],     f = data[, "id"]   )   groups <- paste0("id_", names(persons))   submodels <- lapply(     X = seq_along(persons),     FUN = function(i) {       OpenMx::mxModel(         name = groups[i],         expectation,         OpenMx::mxFitFunctionML(),         OpenMx::mxData(           observed = persons[[i]],           type = "raw"         )       )     }   )   model <- OpenMx::mxModel(     name = name,     matrices,     OpenMx::mxMatrix(       type = "Unit",       nrow = 1,       ncol = 1,       name = "u"     ),     # the first occasion gets the initial condition of the model     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (mu0 - B %*% u),       name = "x0"     ),     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (sigma0 - Q) %*% t(solve(A)),       name = "P0"     ),     submodels,     OpenMx::mxFitFunctionMultigroup(groups = groups)   )   # retries from perturbed starting values only if the first run fails   OpenMx::mxTryHard(     model = model,     extraTries = 5,     silent = TRUE   ) } mx_matrices <- list(   MxMat(     values = matrix(data = c(1, 0, 1, 1), nrow = 2),     labels = "fixed",     name = "A"   ),   MxMat(values = c(0, 0), labels = "fixed", name = "B"),   MxMat(     values = matrix(data = c(1, 0), nrow = 1),     labels = "fixed",     name = "C"   ),   MxMat(values = 0, labels = "fixed", name = "D"),   MxMat(     values = matrix(data = 0, nrow = 2, ncol = 2),     labels = "fixed",     name = "Q"   ),   MxMat(values = theta, labels = "theta", name = "R"),   MxMat(values = mu0, labels = c("mu0_0", "mu0_1"), name = "mu0"),   MxMat(     values = sigma0,     labels = matrix(       data = c(         "sigma0_00", "sigma0_01",         "sigma0_01", "sigma0_11"       ),       nrow = 2     ),     name = "sigma0"   ) ) fit_mx_ssm <- FitMxSSM(   data = data,   observed = "y1",   matrices = mx_matrices,   name = "lin_growth" ) #>  Beginning initial fit attempt Fit attempt 0, fit=83718.2828186554, new current best! (was 83721.0264783941)                                                                               #>  #>  Solution found!  Final fit=83718.283 (started at 83721.026)  (1 attempt(s): 1 valid, 0 errors) summary(fit_mx_ssm) #> Summary of lin_growth  #>   #> free parameters: #>        name matrix row col  Estimate   Std.Error A #> 1     theta      R   1   1 0.5953013 0.006874368   #> 2     mu0_0    mu0   1   1 0.6043436 0.021289172   #> 3     mu0_1    mu0   2   1 0.9984233 0.011286438   #> 4 sigma0_00 sigma0   1   1 1.9097376 0.045538447   #> 5 sigma0_01 sigma0   2   1 0.5926740 0.018313941   #> 6 sigma0_11 sigma0   2   2 0.5773043 0.012755262   #>  #> Model Statistics:  #>                |  Parameters  |  Degrees of Freedom  |  Fit (-2lnL units) #>        Model:              6                  24994              83718.28 #>    Saturated:             NA                     NA                    NA #> Independence:             NA                     NA                    NA #> Number of observations/statistics: 25000/25000 #>  #> Information Criteria:  #>       |  df Penalty  |  Parameters Penalty  |  Sample-Size Adjusted #> AIC:       33730.28               83730.28                 83730.29 #> BIC:     -169386.73               83779.04                 83759.97 #> To get additional fit indices, see help(mxRefModels) #> timestamp: 2026-11-05 05:40:09  #> Wall clock time: 77.01415 secs  #> optimizer:  SLSQP  #> OpenMx version number: 2.22.11  #> Need help? code: EstimatesTable <- function(population, estimate, se, ll = NULL, ul = NULL) {   z <- stats::qnorm(p = 0.975)   if (is.null(ll)) {     ll <- estimate - z * se   }   if (is.null(ul)) {     ul <- estimate + z * se   }   data.frame(     Parameter = names(population),     Population = unname(population),     Estimate = unname(estimate),     SE = unname(se),     Bias = unname(estimate - population),     `2.5%` = unname(ll),     `97.5%` = unname(ul),     Covers = unname(population >= ll & population <= ul),     check.names = FALSE   ) } population <- c(   mu0_0 = mu0[1],   mu0_1 = mu0[2],   sigma0_00 = sigma0[1, 1],   sigma0_01 = sigma0[1, 2],   sigma0_11 = sigma0[2, 2],   theta = theta )

title: The Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Model
text: OpenMx (Neale et al., 2016) fits state space model Kalman filter (OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(); Hunter (2018)). matrices names used engineering: transition matrix \boldsymbol{\beta}, B holds intercepts dynamic model, C loading matrix \boldsymbol{\Lambda}, D holds intercepts measurement model, Q process noise covariance matrix, R measurement error covariance matrix. parameter labels dynr names; dynr, label used two places one shared parameter, starting values population values. Two details differ dynr. First, OpenMx reads data single time series. start filter first occasion every individual, individual gets group, groups use matrices one parent model, every individual parameters. Second, OpenMx starts filter one occasion first row, first row state mean \mathbf{} \mathbf{x}_{0} + \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} state covariance \mathbf{} \mathbf{P}_{0} \mathbf{}^{\prime} + \mathbf{Q}, constant input \mathbf{u} = 1. Setting \mathbf{x}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\mu}_{0} - \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} \right) \mathbf{P}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{0} - \mathbf{Q} \right) \left( \mathbf{}^{-1} \right)^{\prime} gives first occasion initial condition model, likelihood dynr. needs invertible \mathbf{}, holds . two helper functions every vignette package. MxMat() makes OpenMx matrix values dynr-style labels ("fixed" marks fixed element), FitMxSSM() builds groups fits model. model continuous time, discrete-time matrices , B, Q exact discretization drift matrix \boldsymbol{\Phi}, equilibrium \boldsymbol{\mu}, diffusion matrix \boldsymbol{\Sigma} interval \Delta_{t}, written OpenMx algebras: \mathbf{} = \exp \left( \boldsymbol{\Phi} \Delta_{t} \right), \mathbf{B} = \left( \mathbf{} - \mathbf{} \right) \boldsymbol{\mu}, \mathbf{Q} matrix exponential block matrix (Van Loan, 1978). free parameters still \boldsymbol{\Phi}, \boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}, dynr labels. use discrete-time expectation algebras rather OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpaceContinuousTime(): checks OpenMx 2.22.11, process noise covariance interval match exact one \boldsymbol{\Phi} symmetric. matrix exponential omxExponential() algebras also evaluated R, OpenMx attached.
code: MxMat <- function(values, labels, name) {   values <- as.matrix(values)   labels <- matrix(     data = labels,     nrow = nrow(values),     ncol = ncol(values)   )   free <- labels != "fixed"   labels[!free] <- NA   OpenMx::mxMatrix(     type = "Full",     values = values,     free = free,     labels = labels,     name = name   ) } FitMxSSM <- function(data, observed, matrices, name) {   # the groups refer to the matrices of the parent model   shared <- function(x) {     paste0(name, ".", x)   }   expectation <- OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(     A = shared("A"),     B = shared("B"),     C = shared("C"),     D = shared("D"),     Q = shared("Q"),     R = shared("R"),     x0 = shared("x0"),     P0 = shared("P0"),     u = shared("u")   )   # OpenMx needs the names of the observed variables and of the states on C   for (i in seq_along(matrices)) {     if (matrices[[i]]$name == "C") {       dimnames(matrices[[i]]) <- list(         observed,         paste0("eta_", seq_len(ncol(matrices[[i]]$values)))       )     }   }   persons <- split(     x = data[, observed, drop = FALSE],     f = data[, "id"]   )   groups <- paste0("id_", names(persons))   submodels <- lapply(     X = seq_along(persons),     FUN = function(i) {       OpenMx::mxModel(         name = groups[i],         expectation,         OpenMx::mxFitFunctionML(),         OpenMx::mxData(           observed = persons[[i]],           type = "raw"         )       )     }   )   model <- OpenMx::mxModel(     name = name,     matrices,     OpenMx::mxMatrix(       type = "Unit",       nrow = 1,       ncol = 1,       name = "u"     ),     # the first occasion gets the initial condition of the model     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (mu0 - B %*% u),       name = "x0"     ),     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (sigma0 - Q) %*% t(solve(A)),       name = "P0"     ),     submodels,     OpenMx::mxFitFunctionMultigroup(groups = groups)   )   # retries from perturbed starting values only if the first run fails   OpenMx::mxTryHard(     model = model,     extraTries = 5,     silent = TRUE   ) } library(OpenMx) #> To take full advantage of multiple cores, use: #>   mxOption(key='Number of Threads', value=parallel::detectCores()) #now #>   Sys.setenv(OMP_NUM_THREADS=parallel::detectCores()) #before library(OpenMx) labels_phi <- matrix(   data = c(     "phi_1_1", "phi_2_1", "phi_3_1",     "phi_1_2", "phi_2_2", "phi_3_2",     "phi_1_3", "phi_2_3", "phi_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) labels_sigma <- matrix(   data = c(     "sigma_1_1", "sigma_2_1", "sigma_3_1",     "sigma_2_1", "sigma_2_2", "sigma_3_2",     "sigma_3_1", "sigma_3_2", "sigma_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) labels_theta <- matrix(   data = c(     "theta_1_1", "fixed", "fixed",     "fixed", "theta_2_2", "fixed",     "fixed", "fixed", "theta_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) labels_sigma0 <- matrix(   data = c(     "sigma0_1_1", "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_3_1",     "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_2_2", "sigma0_3_2",     "sigma0_3_1", "sigma0_3_2", "sigma0_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) mx_matrices <- list(   MxMat(values = phi, labels = labels_phi, name = "phi"),   MxMat(     values = mu,     labels = c("mu_1_1", "mu_2_1", "mu_3_1"),     name = "mu"   ),   MxMat(values = sigma, labels = labels_sigma, name = "sigma"),   MxMat(values = delta_t, labels = "fixed", name = "delta_t"),   MxMat(values = diag(3), labels = "fixed", name = "I"),   MxMat(     values = matrix(data = 0, nrow = 3, ncol = 3),     labels = "fixed",     name = "Z"   ),   # exact discretization over delta_t   OpenMx::mxAlgebra(     expression = omxExponential(phi * delta_t),     name = "A"   ),   OpenMx::mxAlgebra(     expression = (I - A) %*% mu,     name = "B"   ),   OpenMx::mxAlgebra(     expression = omxExponential(       rbind(cbind(-phi, sigma), cbind(Z, t(phi))) * delta_t     ),     name = "vanloan"   ),   OpenMx::mxAlgebra(     expression = t(vanloan[4:6, 4:6]) %*% vanloan[1:3, 4:6],     name = "Q"   ),   MxMat(values = lambda, labels = "fixed", name = "C"),   MxMat(values = nu, labels = "fixed", name = "D"),   MxMat(values = theta, labels = labels_theta, name = "R"),   MxMat(     values = mu0,     labels = c("mu0_1_1", "mu0_2_1", "mu0_3_1"),     name = "mu0"   ),   MxMat(values = sigma0, labels = labels_sigma0, name = "sigma0") ) fit_mx_ssm <- FitMxSSM(   data = data,   observed = c("y1", "y2", "y3"),   matrices = mx_matrices,   name = "ou" ) #>  Beginning initial fit attempt Fit attempt 0, fit=429162.257745944, new current best! text: table puts population values used simulate data next estimates one method. Bias estimate minus population value. model fitted single simulated data set, error one estimate, Monte Carlo bias, average many replications. 95% confidence interval Wald interval, \hat{\theta} \pm 1.96 \times \mathrm{SE}, unless caption says otherwise, Covers shows whether contains population value. parameter names dynr names every table.
code: EstimatesTable <- function(population, estimate, se, ll = NULL, ul = NULL) {   z <- stats::qnorm(p = 0.975)   if (is.null(ll)) {     ll <- estimate - z * se   }   if (is.null(ul)) {     ul <- estimate + z * se   }   data.frame(     Parameter = names(population),     Population = unname(population),     Estimate = unname(estimate),     SE = unname(se),     Bias = unname(estimate - population),     `2.5%` = unname(ll),     `97.5%` = unname(ul),     Covers = unname(population >= ll & population <= ul),     check.names = FALSE   ) } # the population value for each dynr parameter name, # for example, "beta_1_2" is beta[1, 2] and "mu0_2_1" is mu0[2] population <- vapply(   X = strsplit(x = names(coef(results)), split = "_"),   FUN = function(x) {     as.matrix(get(x[1]))[as.integer(x[2]), as.integer(x[3])]   },   FUN.VALUE = numeric(1) ) names(population) <- names(coef(results))

title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
text: random intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) studies two variables measured individuals several occasions relate time, example, self-esteem depression measured year (Hamaker et al., 2015). individual stable level variable, called trait, fluctuates around occasion occasion. model separates two: traits describe stable differences individuals, cross-lagged effects describe fluctuation one variable followed fluctuation next occasion, within individual. traditional cross-lagged panel model (CLPM) traits, mixes two kinds differences; VAR model vignette vector autoregressive models, fitted panel data. RI-CLPM usually fitted structural equation model (SEM) (Mulder & Hamaker, 2021). can also written state space model: traits latent states never change, within-person components latent states follow vector autoregressive process. tutorial three things: writes RI-CLPM state space model. simulates data model SimSSMFixed(). fits model simulated data state space model dynr OpenMx structural equation model (SEM) lavaan OpenMx, compares every set estimates values used simulate data. prior knowledge state space models needed.

title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
text: fit model dynr, estimates state space models maximum likelihood using Kalman filter. dynr model built pieces match equations : data, initial condition, measurement model, dynamic model, noise. parameter gets name (example, beta_3_4 \beta_{34}), name used two places means one shared parameter. starting values set population values convenience; real data, rough guesses.

title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
text: Tell dynr columns hold individual, time, observed variables.
code: dynr_data <- dynr::dynr.data(   dataframe = data,   id = "id",   time = "time",   observed = c("y1", "y2") )

title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
text: means traits estimated; means within-person components fixed zero. covariance matrix two free blocks, traits within-person components first occasion; covariances blocks fixed zero.
code: dynr_initial <- dynr::prep.initial(   values.inistate = mu0,   params.inistate = c("mu0_1_1", "mu0_2_1", "fixed", "fixed"),   values.inicov = sigma0,   params.inicov = matrix(     data = c(       "sigma0_1_1", "sigma0_2_1", "fixed", "fixed",       "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_2_2", "fixed", "fixed",       "fixed", "fixed", "sigma0_3_3", "sigma0_4_3",       "fixed", "fixed", "sigma0_4_3", "sigma0_4_4"     ),     nrow = 4   ) )

title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
text: loadings fixed: observed variable trait plus within-person component.
code: dynr_measurement <- dynr::prep.measurement(   values.load = lambda,   params.load = matrix(data = "fixed", nrow = 2, ncol = 4),   state.names = c("eta_1", "eta_2", "eta_3", "eta_4"),   obs.names = c("y1", "y2") )

title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
text: formula one row dynamic equation. traits carry unchanged; within-person components autoregressive cross-lagged effects.
code: dynr_dynamics <- dynr::prep.formulaDynamics(   formula = list(     eta_1 ~ eta_1,     eta_2 ~ eta_2,     eta_3 ~ beta_3_3 * eta_3 + beta_3_4 * eta_4,     eta_4 ~ beta_4_3 * eta_3 + beta_4_4 * eta_4   ),   startval = c(     beta_3_3 = beta[3, 3], beta_3_4 = beta[3, 4],     beta_4_3 = beta[4, 3], beta_4_4 = beta[4, 4]   ),   isContinuousTime = FALSE )

title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
text: within-person components process noise. measurement error fixed zero.
code: dynr_noise <- dynr::prep.noise(   values.latent = psi,   params.latent = matrix(     data = c(       "fixed", "fixed", "fixed", "fixed",       "fixed", "fixed", "fixed", "fixed",       "fixed", "fixed", "psi_3_3", "psi_4_3",       "fixed", "fixed", "psi_4_3", "psi_4_4"     ),     nrow = 4   ),   values.observed = theta,   params.observed = matrix(data = "fixed", nrow = 2, ncol = 2) )

title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
text: pieces put together one model. dynr writes model C code outfile compiles . plot shows model equations parameter names.
code: model <- dynr::dynr.model(   data = dynr_data,   initial = dynr_initial,   measurement = dynr_measurement,   dynamics = dynr_dynamics,   noise = dynr_noise,   outfile = "ri-clpm.c" )

title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
text: OpenMx (Neale et al., 2016) fits state space model Kalman filter (OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(); Hunter (2018)). matrices names used engineering: transition matrix \boldsymbol{\beta}, B holds intercepts dynamic model, C loading matrix \boldsymbol{\Lambda}, D holds intercepts measurement model, Q process noise covariance matrix, R measurement error covariance matrix. parameter labels dynr names; dynr, label used two places one shared parameter, starting values population values. Two details differ dynr. First, OpenMx reads data single time series. start filter first occasion every individual, individual gets group, groups use matrices one parent model, every individual parameters. Second, OpenMx starts filter one occasion first row, first row state mean \mathbf{} \mathbf{x}_{0} + \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} state covariance \mathbf{} \mathbf{P}_{0} \mathbf{}^{\prime} + \mathbf{Q}, constant input \mathbf{u} = 1. Setting \mathbf{x}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\mu}_{0} - \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} \right) \mathbf{P}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{0} - \mathbf{Q} \right) \left( \mathbf{}^{-1} \right)^{\prime} gives first occasion initial condition model, likelihood dynr. needs invertible \mathbf{}, holds . two helper functions every vignette package. MxMat() makes OpenMx matrix values dynr-style labels ("fixed" marks fixed element), FitMxSSM() builds groups fits model. matrices model, dynr labels. measurement error (R zero).
code: MxMat <- function(values, labels, name) {   values <- as.matrix(values)   labels <- matrix(     data = labels,     nrow = nrow(values),     ncol = ncol(values)   )   free <- labels != "fixed"   labels[!free] <- NA   OpenMx::mxMatrix(     type = "Full",     values = values,     free = free,     labels = labels,     name = name   ) } FitMxSSM <- function(data, observed, matrices, name) {   # the groups refer to the matrices of the parent model   shared <- function(x) {     paste0(name, ".", x)   }   expectation <- OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(     A = shared("A"),     B = shared("B"),     C = shared("C"),     D = shared("D"),     Q = shared("Q"),     R = shared("R"),     x0 = shared("x0"),     P0 = shared("P0"),     u = shared("u")   )   # OpenMx needs the names of the observed variables and of the states on C   for (i in seq_along(matrices)) {     if (matrices[[i]]$name == "C") {       dimnames(matrices[[i]]) <- list(         observed,         paste0("eta_", seq_len(ncol(matrices[[i]]$values)))       )     }   }   persons <- split(     x = data[, observed, drop = FALSE],     f = data[, "id"]   )   groups <- paste0("id_", names(persons))   submodels <- lapply(     X = seq_along(persons),     FUN = function(i) {       OpenMx::mxModel(         name = groups[i],         expectation,         OpenMx::mxFitFunctionML(),         OpenMx::mxData(           observed = persons[[i]],           type = "raw"         )       )     }   )   model <- OpenMx::mxModel(     name = name,     matrices,     OpenMx::mxMatrix(       type = "Unit",       nrow = 1,       ncol = 1,       name = "u"     ),     # the first occasion gets the initial condition of the model     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (mu0 - B %*% u),       name = "x0"     ),     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (sigma0 - Q) %*% t(solve(A)),       name = "P0"     ),     submodels,     OpenMx::mxFitFunctionMultigroup(groups = groups)   )   # retries from perturbed starting values only if the first run fails   OpenMx::mxTryHard(     model = model,     extraTries = 5,     silent = TRUE   ) } labels_beta <- matrix(data = "fixed", nrow = 4, ncol = 4) labels_beta[3:4, 3:4] <- c("beta_3_3", "beta_4_3", "beta_3_4", "beta_4_4") labels_psi <- matrix(data = "fixed", nrow = 4, ncol = 4) labels_psi[3:4, 3:4] <- c("psi_3_3", "psi_4_3", "psi_4_3", "psi_4_4") labels_sigma0 <- matrix(data = "fixed", nrow = 4, ncol = 4) labels_sigma0[1:2, 1:2] <- c(   "sigma0_1_1", "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_2_2" ) labels_sigma0[3:4, 3:4] <- c(   "sigma0_3_3", "sigma0_4_3", "sigma0_4_3", "sigma0_4_4" ) mx_matrices <- list(   MxMat(values = beta, labels = labels_beta, name = "A"),   MxMat(values = alpha, labels = "fixed", name = "B"),   MxMat(values = lambda, labels = "fixed", name = "C"),   MxMat(values = nu, labels = "fixed", name = "D"),   MxMat(values = psi, labels = labels_psi, name = "Q"),   MxMat(values = theta, labels = "fixed", name = "R"),   MxMat(     values = mu0,     labels = c("mu0_1_1", "mu0_2_1", "fixed", "fixed"),     name = "mu0"   ),   MxMat(values = sigma0, labels = labels_sigma0, name = "sigma0") ) fit_mx_ssm <- FitMxSSM(   data = data,   observed = c("y1", "y2"),   matrices = mx_matrices,   name = "ri_clpm" ) #>  Beginning initial fit attempt Fit attempt 0, fit=123375.561436516, new current best! (was 123393.61516414)                                                                              #>  #>  Solution found!  Final fit=123375.56 (started at 123393.62)  (1 attempt(s): 1 valid, 0 errors) summary(fit_mx_ssm) #> Summary of ri_clpm  #>   #> free parameters: #>          name matrix row col   Estimate   Std.Error A #> 1    beta_3_3      A   3   3 0.50029083 0.012618419   #> 2    beta_4_3      A   4   3 0.08768250 0.010213720   #> 3    beta_3_4      A   3   4 0.14835897 0.010300533   #> 4    beta_4_4      A   4   4 0.38921164 0.012238646   #> 5     psi_3_3      Q   3   3 0.49892137 0.006605229   #> 6     psi_4_3      Q   4   3 0.09056997 0.004771368   #> 7     psi_4_4      Q   4   4 0.48400515 0.006513539   #> 8     mu0_1_1    mu0   1   1 2.97928062 0.016658625   #> 9     mu0_2_1    mu0   2   1 1.99301238 0.015775766   #> 10 sigma0_1_1 sigma0   1   1 1.05970864 0.030935560   #> 11 sigma0_2_1 sigma0   2   1 0.52731732 0.022643329   #> 12 sigma0_2_2 sigma0   2   2 1.01051869 0.026375114   #> 13 sigma0_3_3 sigma0   3   3 0.69592116 0.022937260   #> 14 sigma0_4_3 sigma0   4   3 0.22291390 0.015840671   #> 15 sigma0_4_4 sigma0   4   4 0.62446968 0.018590491   #>  #> Model Statistics:  #>                |  Parameters  |  Degrees of Freedom  |  Fit (-2lnL units) #>        Model:             15                  49985              123375.6 #>    Saturated:             NA                     NA                    NA #> Independence:             NA                     NA                    NA #> Number of observations/statistics: 25000/50000 #>  #> Information Criteria:  #>       |  df Penalty  |  Parameters Penalty  |  Sample-Size Adjusted #> AIC:       23405.56               123405.6                 123405.6 #> BIC:     -382804.09               123527.5                 123479.8 #> To get additional fit indices, see help(mxRefModels) #> timestamp: 2026-11-05 06:37:12  #> Wall clock time: 131.5413 secs  #> optimizer:  SLSQP  #> OpenMx version number: 2.22.11  #> Need help? title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model
text: table puts population values used simulate data next estimates one method. Bias estimate minus population value. model fitted single simulated data set, error one estimate, Monte Carlo bias, average many replications. 95% confidence interval Wald interval, \hat{\theta} \pm 1.96 \times \mathrm{SE}, unless caption says otherwise, Covers shows whether contains population value. parameter names dynr names every table.
code: EstimatesTable <- function(population, estimate, se, ll = NULL, ul = NULL) {   z <- stats::qnorm(p = 0.975)   if (is.null(ll)) {     ll <- estimate - z * se   }   if (is.null(ul)) {     ul <- estimate + z * se   }   data.frame(     Parameter = names(population),     Population = unname(population),     Estimate = unname(estimate),     SE = unname(se),     Bias = unname(estimate - population),     `2.5%` = unname(ll),     `97.5%` = unname(ul),     Covers = unname(population >= ll & population <= ul),     check.names = FALSE   ) } population <- c(   mu0_1_1 = mu0[1],   mu0_2_1 = mu0[2],   sigma0_1_1 = sigma0[1, 1],   sigma0_2_1 = sigma0[2, 1],   sigma0_2_2 = sigma0[2, 2],   sigma0_3_3 = sigma0[3, 3],   sigma0_4_3 = sigma0[4, 3],   sigma0_4_4 = sigma0[4, 4],   beta_3_3 = beta[3, 3],   beta_3_4 = beta[3, 4],   beta_4_3 = beta[4, 3],   beta_4_4 = beta[4, 4],   psi_3_3 = psi[3, 3],   psi_4_3 = psi[4, 3],   psi_4_4 = psi[4, 4] )

title: The State Space Model
text: OpenMx (Neale et al., 2016) fits state space model Kalman filter (OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(); Hunter (2018)). matrices names used engineering: transition matrix \boldsymbol{\beta}, B holds intercepts dynamic model, C loading matrix \boldsymbol{\Lambda}, D holds intercepts measurement model, Q process noise covariance matrix, R measurement error covariance matrix. parameter labels dynr names; dynr, label used two places one shared parameter, starting values population values. Two details differ dynr. First, OpenMx reads data single time series. start filter first occasion every individual, individual gets group, groups use matrices one parent model, every individual parameters. Second, OpenMx starts filter one occasion first row, first row state mean \mathbf{} \mathbf{x}_{0} + \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} state covariance \mathbf{} \mathbf{P}_{0} \mathbf{}^{\prime} + \mathbf{Q}, constant input \mathbf{u} = 1. Setting \mathbf{x}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\mu}_{0} - \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} \right) \mathbf{P}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{0} - \mathbf{Q} \right) \left( \mathbf{}^{-1} \right)^{\prime} gives first occasion initial condition model, likelihood dynr. needs invertible \mathbf{}, holds . two helper functions every vignette package. MxMat() makes OpenMx matrix values dynr-style labels ("fixed" marks fixed element), FitMxSSM() builds groups fits model. matrices model, dynr labels.
code: MxMat <- function(values, labels, name) {   values <- as.matrix(values)   labels <- matrix(     data = labels,     nrow = nrow(values),     ncol = ncol(values)   )   free <- labels != "fixed"   labels[!free] <- NA   OpenMx::mxMatrix(     type = "Full",     values = values,     free = free,     labels = labels,     name = name   ) } FitMxSSM <- function(data, observed, matrices, name) {   # the groups refer to the matrices of the parent model   shared <- function(x) {     paste0(name, ".", x)   }   expectation <- OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(     A = shared("A"),     B = shared("B"),     C = shared("C"),     D = shared("D"),     Q = shared("Q"),     R = shared("R"),     x0 = shared("x0"),     P0 = shared("P0"),     u = shared("u")   )   # OpenMx needs the names of the observed variables and of the states on C   for (i in seq_along(matrices)) {     if (matrices[[i]]$name == "C") {       dimnames(matrices[[i]]) <- list(         observed,         paste0("eta_", seq_len(ncol(matrices[[i]]$values)))       )     }   }   persons <- split(     x = data[, observed, drop = FALSE],     f = data[, "id"]   )   groups <- paste0("id_", names(persons))   submodels <- lapply(     X = seq_along(persons),     FUN = function(i) {       OpenMx::mxModel(         name = groups[i],         expectation,         OpenMx::mxFitFunctionML(),         OpenMx::mxData(           observed = persons[[i]],           type = "raw"         )       )     }   )   model <- OpenMx::mxModel(     name = name,     matrices,     OpenMx::mxMatrix(       type = "Unit",       nrow = 1,       ncol = 1,       name = "u"     ),     # the first occasion gets the initial condition of the model     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (mu0 - B %*% u),       name = "x0"     ),     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (sigma0 - Q) %*% t(solve(A)),       name = "P0"     ),     submodels,     OpenMx::mxFitFunctionMultigroup(groups = groups)   )   # retries from perturbed starting values only if the first run fails   OpenMx::mxTryHard(     model = model,     extraTries = 5,     silent = TRUE   ) } labels_beta <- matrix(   data = c(     "beta_1_1", "beta_2_1", "beta_3_1",     "beta_1_2", "beta_2_2", "beta_3_2",     "beta_1_3", "beta_2_3", "beta_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) labels_psi <- matrix(   data = c(     "psi_1_1", "psi_2_1", "psi_3_1",     "psi_2_1", "psi_2_2", "psi_3_2",     "psi_3_1", "psi_3_2", "psi_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) labels_theta <- matrix(   data = c(     "theta_1_1", "fixed", "fixed",     "fixed", "theta_2_2", "fixed",     "fixed", "fixed", "theta_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) labels_sigma0 <- matrix(   data = c(     "sigma0_1_1", "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_3_1",     "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_2_2", "sigma0_3_2",     "sigma0_3_1", "sigma0_3_2", "sigma0_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) mx_matrices <- list(   MxMat(values = beta, labels = labels_beta, name = "A"),   MxMat(     values = alpha,     labels = c("alpha_1_1", "alpha_2_1", "alpha_3_1"),     name = "B"   ),   MxMat(values = lambda, labels = "fixed", name = "C"),   MxMat(values = nu, labels = "fixed", name = "D"),   MxMat(values = psi, labels = labels_psi, name = "Q"),   MxMat(values = theta, labels = labels_theta, name = "R"),   MxMat(     values = mu0,     labels = c("mu0_1_1", "mu0_2_1", "mu0_3_1"),     name = "mu0"   ),   MxMat(values = sigma0, labels = labels_sigma0, name = "sigma0") ) fit_mx_ssm <- FitMxSSM(   data = data,   observed = c("y1", "y2", "y3"),   matrices = mx_matrices,   name = "ssm" ) #>  Beginning initial fit attempt Fit attempt 0, fit=530766.196230886, new current best! (was 530781.853350924)                                                                               #>  #>  Solution found! code: EstimatesTable <- function(population, estimate, se, ll = NULL, ul = NULL) {   z <- stats::qnorm(p = 0.975)   if (is.null(ll)) {     ll <- estimate - z * se   }   if (is.null(ul)) {     ul <- estimate + z * se   }   data.frame(     Parameter = names(population),     Population = unname(population),     Estimate = unname(estimate),     SE = unname(se),     Bias = unname(estimate - population),     `2.5%` = unname(ll),     `97.5%` = unname(ul),     Covers = unname(population >= ll & population <= ul),     check.names = FALSE   ) } # the population value for each dynr parameter name, # for example, "beta_1_2" is beta[1, 2] and "mu0_2_1" is mu0[2] population <- vapply(   X = strsplit(x = names(coef(results)), split = "_"),   FUN = function(x) {     as.matrix(get(x[1]))[as.integer(x[2]), as.integer(x[3])]   },   FUN.VALUE = numeric(1) ) names(population) <- names(coef(results))

title: The Stable Trait, Autoregressive Trait, and State Model
text: OpenMx (Neale et al., 2016) fits state space model Kalman filter (OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(); Hunter (2018)). matrices names used engineering: transition matrix \boldsymbol{\beta}, B holds intercepts dynamic model, C loading matrix \boldsymbol{\Lambda}, D holds intercepts measurement model, Q process noise covariance matrix, R measurement error covariance matrix. parameter labels dynr names; dynr, label used two places one shared parameter, starting values population values. Two details differ dynr. First, OpenMx reads data single time series. start filter first occasion every individual, individual gets group, groups use matrices one parent model, every individual parameters. Second, OpenMx starts filter one occasion first row, first row state mean \mathbf{} \mathbf{x}_{0} + \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} state covariance \mathbf{} \mathbf{P}_{0} \mathbf{}^{\prime} + \mathbf{Q}, constant input \mathbf{u} = 1. Setting \mathbf{x}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\mu}_{0} - \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} \right) \mathbf{P}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{0} - \mathbf{Q} \right) \left( \mathbf{}^{-1} \right)^{\prime} gives first occasion initial condition model, likelihood dynr. needs invertible \mathbf{}, holds . two helper functions every vignette package. MxMat() makes OpenMx matrix values dynr-style labels ("fixed" marks fixed element), FitMxSSM() builds groups fits model. matrices model, dynr labels.
code: MxMat <- function(values, labels, name) {   values <- as.matrix(values)   labels <- matrix(     data = labels,     nrow = nrow(values),     ncol = ncol(values)   )   free <- labels != "fixed"   labels[!free] <- NA   OpenMx::mxMatrix(     type = "Full",     values = values,     free = free,     labels = labels,     name = name   ) } FitMxSSM <- function(data, observed, matrices, name) {   # the groups refer to the matrices of the parent model   shared <- function(x) {     paste0(name, ".", x)   }   expectation <- OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(     A = shared("A"),     B = shared("B"),     C = shared("C"),     D = shared("D"),     Q = shared("Q"),     R = shared("R"),     x0 = shared("x0"),     P0 = shared("P0"),     u = shared("u")   )   # OpenMx needs the names of the observed variables and of the states on C   for (i in seq_along(matrices)) {     if (matrices[[i]]$name == "C") {       dimnames(matrices[[i]]) <- list(         observed,         paste0("eta_", seq_len(ncol(matrices[[i]]$values)))       )     }   }   persons <- split(     x = data[, observed, drop = FALSE],     f = data[, "id"]   )   groups <- paste0("id_", names(persons))   submodels <- lapply(     X = seq_along(persons),     FUN = function(i) {       OpenMx::mxModel(         name = groups[i],         expectation,         OpenMx::mxFitFunctionML(),         OpenMx::mxData(           observed = persons[[i]],           type = "raw"         )       )     }   )   model <- OpenMx::mxModel(     name = name,     matrices,     OpenMx::mxMatrix(       type = "Unit",       nrow = 1,       ncol = 1,       name = "u"     ),     # the first occasion gets the initial condition of the model     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (mu0 - B %*% u),       name = "x0"     ),     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (sigma0 - Q) %*% t(solve(A)),       name = "P0"     ),     submodels,     OpenMx::mxFitFunctionMultigroup(groups = groups)   )   # retries from perturbed starting values only if the first run fails   OpenMx::mxTryHard(     model = model,     extraTries = 5,     silent = TRUE   ) } mx_matrices <- list(   MxMat(     values = beta,     labels = c("fixed", "fixed", "fixed", "beta_2_2"),     name = "A"   ),   MxMat(values = alpha, labels = "fixed", name = "B"),   MxMat(values = lambda, labels = "fixed", name = "C"),   MxMat(values = nu, labels = "fixed", name = "D"),   MxMat(     values = psi,     labels = c("fixed", "fixed", "fixed", "psi_2_2"),     name = "Q"   ),   MxMat(values = theta, labels = "theta", name = "R"),   MxMat(values = mu0, labels = c("mu0_1_1", "fixed"), name = "mu0"),   MxMat(     values = sigma0,     labels = c("sigma0_1_1", "fixed", "fixed", "sigma0_2_2"),     name = "sigma0"   ) ) fit_mx_ssm <- FitMxSSM(   data = data,   observed = "y1",   matrices = mx_matrices,   name = "starts" ) #>  Beginning initial fit attempt Fit attempt 0, fit=130172.19038846, new current best! title: The Vector Autoregressive Model
text: measurement model given \mathbf{y}_{, t}   =   \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t} \mathbf{y}_{, t} represents vector observed variables \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t} vector latent variables individual time t. Since observed latent variables equal, generate data dynamic structure. dynamic structure given \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}   =   \boldsymbol{\alpha}   +   \boldsymbol{\beta}   \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1}   +   \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t},   \quad   \mathrm{}   \quad   \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}   \sim   \mathcal{N}   \left(   \mathbf{0},   \boldsymbol{\Psi}   \right) \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}, \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1}, \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t} random variables, \boldsymbol{\alpha}, \boldsymbol{\beta}, \boldsymbol{\Psi} model parameters. , \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t} vector latent variables time t individual , \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1} represents vector latent variables time t - 1 individual , \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t} represents vector dynamic noise time t individual . \boldsymbol{\alpha} denotes vector intercepts, \boldsymbol{\beta} matrix autoregression cross regression coefficients, \boldsymbol{\Psi} covariance matrix \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}. words, variable time t weighted sum variables time t - 1, plus intercept random shock. weights elements \boldsymbol{\beta}: diagonal element \beta_{jj} autoregressive effect, much variable j carries next occasion. Values closer 1 mean variable changes slowly (high inertia). -diagonal element \beta_{jk} cross-lagged effect variable k time t - 1 variable j time t. Note order: row outcome, column predictor. shocks \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t} stand everything moves variables model explain, example, events happen occasions. process settle around stable mean, eigenvalues \boldsymbol{\beta} must modulus less 1. alternative representation dynamic noise given \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}   =   \boldsymbol{\Psi}^{\frac{1}{2}}   \mathbf{z}_{, t},   \quad   \mathrm{}   \quad   \mathbf{z}_{, t}   \sim   \mathcal{N}   \left(   \mathbf{0},   \mathbf{}   \right) \left( \boldsymbol{\Psi}^{\frac{1}{2}} \right) \left( \boldsymbol{\Psi}^{\frac{1}{2}} \right)^{\prime} = \boldsymbol{\Psi} . noise simulated: independent standard normal draws \mathbf{z}_{, t} multiplied square root \boldsymbol{\Psi}. functions simStateSpace take square root, lower triangular Cholesky factor \boldsymbol{\Psi}, argument psi_l.

title: The Vector Autoregressive Model
text: OpenMx (Neale et al., 2016) fits state space model Kalman filter (OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(); Hunter (2018)). matrices names used engineering: transition matrix \boldsymbol{\beta}, B holds intercepts dynamic model, C loading matrix \boldsymbol{\Lambda}, D holds intercepts measurement model, Q process noise covariance matrix, R measurement error covariance matrix. parameter labels dynr names; dynr, label used two places one shared parameter, starting values population values. Two details differ dynr. First, OpenMx reads data single time series. start filter first occasion every individual, individual gets group, groups use matrices one parent model, every individual parameters. Second, OpenMx starts filter one occasion first row, first row state mean \mathbf{} \mathbf{x}_{0} + \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} state covariance \mathbf{} \mathbf{P}_{0} \mathbf{}^{\prime} + \mathbf{Q}, constant input \mathbf{u} = 1. Setting \mathbf{x}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\mu}_{0} - \mathbf{B} \mathbf{u} \right) \mathbf{P}_{0} = \mathbf{}^{-1} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{0} - \mathbf{Q} \right) \left( \mathbf{}^{-1} \right)^{\prime} gives first occasion initial condition model, likelihood dynr. needs invertible \mathbf{}, holds . two helper functions every vignette package. MxMat() makes OpenMx matrix values dynr-style labels ("fixed" marks fixed element), FitMxSSM() builds groups fits model. matrices model, dynr labels. loadings identity matrix, measurement error (R zero).
code: MxMat <- function(values, labels, name) {   values <- as.matrix(values)   labels <- matrix(     data = labels,     nrow = nrow(values),     ncol = ncol(values)   )   free <- labels != "fixed"   labels[!free] <- NA   OpenMx::mxMatrix(     type = "Full",     values = values,     free = free,     labels = labels,     name = name   ) } FitMxSSM <- function(data, observed, matrices, name) {   # the groups refer to the matrices of the parent model   shared <- function(x) {     paste0(name, ".", x)   }   expectation <- OpenMx::mxExpectationStateSpace(     A = shared("A"),     B = shared("B"),     C = shared("C"),     D = shared("D"),     Q = shared("Q"),     R = shared("R"),     x0 = shared("x0"),     P0 = shared("P0"),     u = shared("u")   )   # OpenMx needs the names of the observed variables and of the states on C   for (i in seq_along(matrices)) {     if (matrices[[i]]$name == "C") {       dimnames(matrices[[i]]) <- list(         observed,         paste0("eta_", seq_len(ncol(matrices[[i]]$values)))       )     }   }   persons <- split(     x = data[, observed, drop = FALSE],     f = data[, "id"]   )   groups <- paste0("id_", names(persons))   submodels <- lapply(     X = seq_along(persons),     FUN = function(i) {       OpenMx::mxModel(         name = groups[i],         expectation,         OpenMx::mxFitFunctionML(),         OpenMx::mxData(           observed = persons[[i]],           type = "raw"         )       )     }   )   model <- OpenMx::mxModel(     name = name,     matrices,     OpenMx::mxMatrix(       type = "Unit",       nrow = 1,       ncol = 1,       name = "u"     ),     # the first occasion gets the initial condition of the model     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (mu0 - B %*% u),       name = "x0"     ),     OpenMx::mxAlgebra(       expression = solve(A) %*% (sigma0 - Q) %*% t(solve(A)),       name = "P0"     ),     submodels,     OpenMx::mxFitFunctionMultigroup(groups = groups)   )   # retries from perturbed starting values only if the first run fails   OpenMx::mxTryHard(     model = model,     extraTries = 5,     silent = TRUE   ) } labels_beta <- matrix(   data = c(     "beta_1_1", "beta_2_1", "beta_3_1",     "beta_1_2", "beta_2_2", "beta_3_2",     "beta_1_3", "beta_2_3", "beta_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) labels_psi <- matrix(   data = c(     "psi_1_1", "psi_2_1", "psi_3_1",     "psi_2_1", "psi_2_2", "psi_3_2",     "psi_3_1", "psi_3_2", "psi_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) labels_sigma0 <- matrix(   data = c(     "sigma0_1_1", "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_3_1",     "sigma0_2_1", "sigma0_2_2", "sigma0_3_2",     "sigma0_3_1", "sigma0_3_2", "sigma0_3_3"   ),   nrow = 3 ) mx_matrices <- list(   MxMat(values = beta, labels = labels_beta, name = "A"),   MxMat(     values = alpha,     labels = c("alpha_1_1", "alpha_2_1", "alpha_3_1"),     name = "B"   ),   MxMat(values = diag(3), labels = "fixed", name = "C"),   MxMat(values = rep(x = 0, times = 3), labels = "fixed", name = "D"),   MxMat(values = psi, labels = labels_psi, name = "Q"),   MxMat(     values = matrix(data = 0, nrow = 3, ncol = 3),     labels = "fixed",     name = "R"   ),   MxMat(     values = mu0,     labels = c("mu0_1_1", "mu0_2_1", "mu0_3_1"),     name = "mu0"   ),   MxMat(values = sigma0, labels = labels_sigma0, name = "sigma0") ) fit_mx_ssm <- FitMxSSM(   data = data,   observed = c("y1", "y2", "y3"),   matrices = mx_matrices,   name = "var" ) #>  Beginning initial fit attempt Fit attempt 0, fit=160369.869850976, new current best! code: EstimatesTable <- function(population, estimate, se, ll = NULL, ul = NULL) {   z <- stats::qnorm(p = 0.975)   if (is.null(ll)) {     ll <- estimate - z * se   }   if (is.null(ul)) {     ul <- estimate + z * se   }   data.frame(     Parameter = names(population),     Population = unname(population),     Estimate = unname(estimate),     SE = unname(se),     Bias = unname(estimate - population),     `2.5%` = unname(ll),     `97.5%` = unname(ul),     Covers = unname(population >= ll & population <= ul),     check.names = FALSE   ) } # the population value for each dynr parameter name, # for example, "beta_1_2" is beta[1, 2] and "mu0_2_1" is mu0[2] population <- vapply(   X = strsplit(x = names(coef(results)), split = "_"),   FUN = function(x) {     as.matrix(get(x[1]))[as.integer(x[2]), as.integer(x[3])]   },   FUN.VALUE = numeric(1) ) names(population) <- names(coef(results))

what: Convert Linear SDE Parameters to State Space Parameters — LinSDE2SSM
title: Convert Linear SDE Parameters to State Space Parameters — LinSDE2SSM
text: function converts linear stochastic differential equation (SDE) parameters discrete-time state space model parameters exact discretization specified sampling interval.

title: Convert Linear SDE Parameters to State Space Parameters — LinSDE2SSM
code: LinSDE2SSM(iota, phi, sigma_l, delta_t = 1)

title: Convert Linear SDE Parameters to State Space Parameters — LinSDE2SSM
text: iota Numeric vector length \(q\). unobserved term constant time (\(\boldsymbol{\iota}\)). phi Numeric \(q \times q\) matrix. drift matrix represents rate change solution absence random fluctuations (\(\boldsymbol{\Phi}\)). sigma_l Numeric \(q \times q\) matrix. Lower triangular factor continuous-time diffusion covariance: sigma_l %*% t(sigma_l). positive-definite covariance matrix sigma, use t(chol(sigma)). factor must lower triangular non-negative diagonal. Zero positive-semidefinite covariances allowed. delta_t Positive finite numeric scalar. Sampling interval \(\Delta t\).

title: Convert Linear SDE Parameters to State Space Parameters — LinSDE2SSM
text: Returns list state space parameters: alpha: Numeric vector. Vector constant values dynamic model (\(\boldsymbol{\alpha}\)). beta: Numeric matrix. Transition matrix relating values latent variables previous time point current time point (\(\boldsymbol{\beta}\)). psi_l: Numeric matrix. Lower triangular factor process noise covariance matrix \(\boldsymbol{\Psi}\).

title: Convert Linear SDE Parameters to State Space Parameters — LinSDE2SSM
text: linear stochastic differential equation $$   \mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\eta}(t)   = (\boldsymbol{\iota} + \boldsymbol{\Phi}\boldsymbol{\eta}(t))     \mathrm{d}t + \mathbf{L}\,\mathrm{d}\mathbf{W}(t), $$ \(\mathbf{L}\) sigma_l \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = \mathbf{L}\mathbf{L}^{\prime}\). sampling interval \(\Delta t\), state equation $$   \boldsymbol{\eta}(t + \Delta t)   = \boldsymbol{\alpha} + \boldsymbol{\beta}\boldsymbol{\eta}(t)     + \boldsymbol{\zeta}(t),   \qquad \boldsymbol{\zeta}(t) \sim   \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Psi}). $$ exact discrete-time parameters $$   \boldsymbol{\beta} = \exp(\Delta t\boldsymbol{\Phi}),   \qquad   \boldsymbol{\alpha} = \left[\int_0^{\Delta t}     \exp(s\boldsymbol{\Phi})\,\mathrm{d}s\right]\boldsymbol{\iota}, $$ $$   \boldsymbol{\Psi} = \int_0^{\Delta t}     \exp(s\boldsymbol{\Phi})\boldsymbol{\Sigma}     \exp(s\boldsymbol{\Phi}^{\prime})\,\mathrm{d}s. $$ implementation evaluates integrals using block matrix exponentials, zero singular drift matrices supported. inputs must contain finite values compatible dimensions.

title: Convert Linear SDE Parameters to State Space Parameters — LinSDE2SSM
text: Harvey, . C. (1990). Forecasting, structural time series models Kalman filter. Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/cbo9781107049994

title: Convert State Space Parameters to Linear SDE Parameters — SSM2LinSDE
text: alpha Numeric vector length \(q\). Intercept discrete-time state equation. beta Numeric \(q \times q\) matrix. Transition matrix discrete-time state equation. psi_l Numeric \(q \times q\) matrix. Lower triangular factor interval process noise covariance: psi_l %*% t(psi_l). positive-definite covariance matrix psi, use t(chol(psi)). Zero positive-semidefinite covariances allowed. delta_t Positive finite numeric scalar. Sampling interval \(\Delta t\). tol Non-negative finite numeric scalar. Tolerance largest absolute imaginary component matrix logarithm. tol_psi_l Non-negative finite numeric scalar. Tolerance checking psi_l lower triangular non-negative diagonal.

title: Convert State Space Parameters to Linear SDE Parameters — SSM2LinSDE
text: Returns list linear stochastic differential equation model parameters: iota: Numeric vector. unobserved term constant time \(\boldsymbol{\iota}\). phi: Numeric matrix. drift matrix represents rate change solution absence random fluctuations \(\boldsymbol{\Phi}\). sigma_l: Numeric matrix. Lower triangular factor covariance matrix volatility randomness process \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\).

title: Convert State Space Parameters to Linear SDE Parameters — SSM2LinSDE
text: state equation continuous-time counterpart described LinSDE2SSM(). drift matrix computed using principal matrix logarithm: $$   \boldsymbol{\Phi} = \frac{1}{\Delta t}\log(\boldsymbol{\beta}). $$ intercept diffusion covariance recovered solving $$   \boldsymbol{\alpha} = \left[\int_0^{\Delta t}     \exp(s\boldsymbol{\Phi})\,\mathrm{d}s\right]\boldsymbol{\iota} $$ $$   \boldsymbol{\Psi} = \int_0^{\Delta t}     \exp(s\boldsymbol{\Phi})\boldsymbol{\Sigma}     \exp(s\boldsymbol{\Phi}^{\prime})\,\mathrm{d}s, $$ psi_l %*% t(psi_l) gives \(\boldsymbol{\Psi}\). integrated exponential operators support zero singular drifts. principal matrix-logarithm branch search possible continuous-time embeddings resolve temporal aliasing. Inputs rejected logarithm finite (singular beta), imaginary component exceeding tol, integral inversions unique, recovered diffusion covariance positive semidefinite. inputs must contain finite values compatible dimensions.

title: Convert State Space Parameters to Linear SDE Parameters — SSM2LinSDE
text: Harvey, . C. (1990). Forecasting, structural time series models Kalman filter. Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/cbo9781107049994

title: Convert State Space Parameters to Linear SDE Parameters — SSM2LinSDE
text: Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

title: Convert State Space Parameters to Linear SDE Parameters — SSM2LinSDE
code: # Example 1: Recover the parameters of a bivariate linear SDE iota <- c(0.32, 0.23)  phi <- matrix(   data = c(     -0.10, 0.05,     0.05, -0.10   ),   nrow = 2 )  sigma <- matrix(   data = c(     2.79, 0.06,     0.06, 3.27   ),   nrow = 2 )  sigma_l <- t(chol(sigma)) delta_t <- 1.0  ssm <- LinSDE2SSM(   iota = iota,   phi = phi,   sigma_l = sigma_l,   delta_t = delta_t )  SSM2LinSDE(   alpha = ssm$alpha,   beta = ssm$beta,   psi_l = ssm$psi_l,   delta_t = delta_t ) #> $iota #>      [,1] #> [1,] 0.32 #> [2,] 0.23 #>  #> $phi #>       [,1]  [,2] #> [1,] -0.10  0.05 #> [2,]  0.05 -0.10 #>  #> $sigma_l #>            [,1]     [,2] #> [1,] 1.67032931 0.000000 #> [2,] 0.03592106 1.807957 #>

title: Simulate Data from a State Space Model (Fixed Parameters) — SimSSMFixed
code: # prepare parameters set.seed(42) ## number of individuals n <- 5 ## time points time <- 50 ## dynamic structure p <- 3 mu0 <- rep(x = 0, times = p) sigma0 <- 0.001 * diag(p) sigma0_l <- t(chol(sigma0)) alpha <- rep(x = 0, times = p) beta <- 0.50 * diag(p) psi <- 0.001 * diag(p) psi_l <- t(chol(psi)) ## measurement model k <- 3 nu <- rep(x = 0, times = k) lambda <- diag(k) theta <- 0.001 * diag(k) theta_l <- t(chol(theta)) ## covariates j <- 2 x <- lapply(   X = seq_len(n),   FUN = function(i) {     matrix(       data = stats::rnorm(n = time * j),       nrow = j,       ncol = time     )   } ) gamma <- diag(x = 0.10, nrow = p, ncol = j) kappa <- diag(x = 0.10, nrow = k, ncol = j)  # Type 0 ssm <- SimSSMFixed(   n = n,   time = time,   mu0 = mu0,   sigma0_l = sigma0_l,   alpha = alpha,   beta = beta,   psi_l = psi_l,   nu = nu,   lambda = lambda,   theta_l = theta_l,   type = 0 )  plot(ssm)     # Type 1 ssm <- SimSSMFixed(   n = n,   time = time,   mu0 = mu0,   sigma0_l = sigma0_l,   alpha = alpha,   beta = beta,   psi_l = psi_l,   nu = nu,   lambda = lambda,   theta_l = theta_l,   type = 1,   x = x,   gamma = gamma )  plot(ssm)     # Type 2 ssm <- SimSSMFixed(   n = n,   time = time,   mu0 = mu0,   sigma0_l = sigma0_l,   alpha = alpha,   beta = beta,   psi_l = psi_l,   nu = nu,   lambda = lambda,   theta_l = theta_l,   type = 2,   x = x,   gamma = gamma,   kappa = kappa )  plot(ssm)

code: # prepare parameters # In this example, beta varies across individuals. set.seed(42) ## number of individuals n <- 5 ## time points time <- 50 ## dynamic structure p <- 3 mu0 <- list(   rep(x = 0, times = p) ) sigma0 <- 0.001 * diag(p) sigma0_l <- list(   t(chol(sigma0)) ) alpha <- list(   rep(x = 0, times = p) ) beta <- list(   0.1 * diag(p),   0.2 * diag(p),   0.3 * diag(p),   0.4 * diag(p),   0.5 * diag(p) ) psi <- 0.001 * diag(p) psi_l <- list(   t(chol(psi)) ) ## measurement model k <- 3 nu <- list(   rep(x = 0, times = k) ) lambda <- list(   diag(k) ) theta <- 0.001 * diag(k) theta_l <- list(   t(chol(theta)) ) ## covariates j <- 2 x <- lapply(   X = seq_len(n),   FUN = function(i) {     matrix(       data = stats::rnorm(n = time * j),       nrow = j,       ncol = time     )   } ) gamma <- list(   diag(x = 0.10, nrow = p, ncol = j) ) kappa <- list(   diag(x = 0.10, nrow = k, ncol = j) )  # Type 0 ssm <- SimSSMIVary(   n = n,   time = time,   mu0 = mu0,   sigma0_l = sigma0_l,   alpha = alpha,   beta = beta,   psi_l = psi_l,   nu = nu,   lambda = lambda,   theta_l = theta_l,   type = 0 )  plot(ssm)     # Type 1 ssm <- SimSSMIVary(   n = n,   time = time,   mu0 = mu0,   sigma0_l = sigma0_l,   alpha = alpha,   beta = beta,   psi_l = psi_l,   nu = nu,   lambda = lambda,   theta_l = theta_l,   type = 1,   x = x,   gamma = gamma )  plot(ssm)     # Type 2 ssm <- SimSSMIVary(   n = n,   time = time,   mu0 = mu0,   sigma0_l = sigma0_l,   alpha = alpha,   beta = beta,   psi_l = psi_l,   nu = nu,   lambda = lambda,   theta_l = theta_l,   type = 2,   x = x,   gamma = gamma,   kappa = kappa )  plot(ssm)

title: Simulate Data from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Model using a State Space Model Parameterization (Individual-Varying Parameters) — SimSSMOUIVary
code: # prepare parameters # In this example, phi varies across individuals. set.seed(42) ## number of individuals n <- 5 ## time points time <- 50 delta_t <- 0.10 ## dynamic structure p <- 2 mu0 <- list(   c(-3.0, 1.5) ) sigma0 <- 0.001 * diag(p) sigma0_l <- list(   t(chol(sigma0)) ) mu <- list(   c(5.76, 5.18) ) phi <- list(   -0.1 * diag(p),   -0.2 * diag(p),   -0.3 * diag(p),   -0.4 * diag(p),   -0.5 * diag(p) ) sigma <- matrix(   data = c(     2.79,     0.06,     0.06,     3.27   ),   nrow = p ) sigma_l <- list(   t(chol(sigma)) ) ## measurement model k <- 2 nu <- list(   rep(x = 0, times = k) ) lambda <- list(   diag(k) ) theta <- 0.001 * diag(k) theta_l <- list(   t(chol(theta)) ) ## covariates j <- 2 x <- lapply(   X = seq_len(n),   FUN = function(i) {     matrix(       data = stats::rnorm(n = time * j),       nrow = j,       ncol = time     )   } ) gamma <- list(   diag(x = 0.10, nrow = p, ncol = j) ) kappa <- list(   diag(x = 0.10, nrow = k, ncol = j) )  # Type 0 ssm <- SimSSMOUIVary(   n = n,   time = time,   delta_t = delta_t,   mu0 = mu0,   sigma0_l = sigma0_l,   mu = mu,   phi = phi,   sigma_l = sigma_l,   nu = nu,   lambda = lambda,   theta_l = theta_l,   type = 0 )  plot(ssm)    # Type 1 ssm <- SimSSMOUIVary(   n = n,   time = time,   delta_t = delta_t,   mu0 = mu0,   sigma0_l = sigma0_l,   mu = mu,   phi = phi,   sigma_l = sigma_l,   nu = nu,   lambda = lambda,   theta_l = theta_l,   type = 1,   x = x,   gamma = gamma )  plot(ssm)    # Type 2 ssm <- SimSSMOUIVary(   n = n,   time = time,   delta_t = delta_t,   mu0 = mu0,   sigma0_l = sigma0_l,   mu = mu,   phi = phi,   sigma_l = sigma_l,   nu = nu,   lambda = lambda,   theta_l = theta_l,   type = 2,   x = x,   gamma = gamma,   kappa = kappa )  plot(ssm)

title: Simulate Data from the Vector Autoregressive Model (Fixed Parameters) — SimSSMVARFixed
text: measurement model given $$     \mathbf{y}_{, t}     =     \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}   $$ \(\mathbf{y}_{, t}\) represents vector observed variables \(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}\) vector latent variables individual \(\) time \(t\). Since observed latent variables equal, generate data dynamic structure. dynamic structure given $$     \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}     =     \boldsymbol{\alpha}     +     \boldsymbol{\beta}     \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1}     +     \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t},     \quad     \mathrm{}     \quad     \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}     \sim     \mathcal{N}     \left(     \mathbf{0},     \boldsymbol{\Psi}     \right)   $$ \(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}\), \(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1}\), \(\boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}\) random variables, \(\boldsymbol{\alpha}\), \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\), \(\boldsymbol{\Psi}\) model parameters. , \(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}\) vector latent variables time \(t\) individual \(\), \(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1}\) represents vector latent variables time \(t - 1\) individual \(\), \(\boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}\) represents vector dynamic noise time \(t\) individual \(\). \(\boldsymbol{\alpha}\) denotes vector intercepts, \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\) matrix autoregression cross regression coefficients, \(\boldsymbol{\Psi}\) covariance matrix \(\boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}\). alternative representation dynamic noise given $$     \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}     =     \boldsymbol{\Psi}^{\frac{1}{2}}     \mathbf{z}_{, t},     \quad     \mathrm{}     \quad     \mathbf{z}_{, t}     \sim     \mathcal{N}     \left(     \mathbf{0},     \mathbf{}     \right)   $$ \(     \left( \boldsymbol{\Psi}^{\frac{1}{2}} \right)     \left( \boldsymbol{\Psi}^{\frac{1}{2}} \right)^{\prime}     =     \boldsymbol{\Psi} .   \)

title: Simulate Data from the Vector Autoregressive Model (Fixed Parameters) — SimSSMVARFixed
text: measurement model given $$     \mathbf{y}_{, t}     =     \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t} .   $$ dynamic structure given $$     \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}     =     \boldsymbol{\alpha}     +     \boldsymbol{\beta}     \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1}     +     \boldsymbol{\Gamma}     \mathbf{x}_{, t}     +     \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t},     \quad     \mathrm{}     \quad     \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}     \sim     \mathcal{N}     \left(     \mathbf{0},     \boldsymbol{\Psi}     \right)   $$ \(\mathbf{x}_{, t}\) represents vector covariates time \(t\) individual \(\), \(\boldsymbol{\Gamma}\) coefficient matrix linking covariates latent variables.

title: simStateSpace 1.2.17
text: Added ExpMat() LogMat() matrix exponentials real principal matrix logarithms, CompanionMat() VAR block companion matrices. Added CTVAR2SSM() exact sampling higher-order derivative states SSM2LinSDE() continuous-time recovery using principal matrix logarithm, checks uniquely recoverable intercepts positive-semidefinite diffusion. Updated LinSDE2SSM() integrate intercepts diffusion block matrix exponentials, supporting singular drifts semidefinite noise. Covariance integration uses interval subdivision avoid overflow strongly decaying drifts. Added LinSDECovDeltaT() process noise covariance accumulated sampling interval linear SDE model. LinSDE2SSM(): delta_t now defaults 1. SSM2LinSDE() rejects singular beta (non-finite matrix logarithm) separate tolerance, tol_psi_l, checking psi_l lower triangular; tol now applies imaginary part matrix logarithm. Semidefinite noise covariances factored eigendecomposition, LinSDE2SSM() SSM2LinSDE() longer reject rank-deficient covariances rounding error. Added input validation linear SDE mean, covariance, intercept functions expanded transformation tests analytic reference cases. Fixed SSMInterceptY() LinSDEInterceptY(), returned mean_y + lambda %*% mean_eta instead mean_y - lambda %*% mean_eta (since 1.2.15). Replaced Monte Carlo smoke tests exact references: simulators checked plain R state space recursion, moment functions defining equations. Fixed SimSSMLinSDEIVary() SimSSMOUIVary() failing singular drifts, semidefinite diffusion, undamped oscillators: now discretize LinSDE2SSM(), per distinct parameter set. Sim* functions now share one simulation kernel one set input checks, informative errors invalid dimensions, non-finite values, missing covariates. seed gives data . .data.frame() long = FALSE (wide format) faster balanced data; columns . Help pages SimSSMFixed(), SimSSMIVary(), SimSSMLinGrowth(), functions inherit arguments write mean vector covariance matrix initial condition mu_0 Sigma_0 (mu_{eta | 0} Sigma_{eta | 0}), vignettes .
